title: docs(fretboard): correct the slot_width_mm field description - it is a slot, not a tang
intent: FretboardInput.slot_width_mm described its 0.58mm default as a 'medium fret wire tang'. It is a slot width, not a tang width, and the part it cited (StewMac 0148) is the vintage_medium profile rather than medium. The wrong word is not cosmetic: comparing this slot against fret_wire_calc.FRET_WIRE_CATALOG's tang_width_mm (medium 0.53 / jumbo 0.58) makes the two registries look like they disagree about which wire the default is for, and that false conflict was reported as a finding before it was traced. Description text only - the default and its bounds are untouched.

diff_articulation.what_changed: One Field description rewritten and a nine-line comment added above it. The new description sources 0.58mm to fret_wire_physics.FRET_PROFILES, where slot_width_in is 0.023in for medium wire (StewMac 150 / Dunlop 6160) and for every lighter profile, and notes that only 'jumbo' needs 0.025in / 0.635mm. It states explicitly that this is the slot and not the tang, and gives the medium tang as 0.53mm so the two registries cannot be conflated again. The 'Jescar 47104' citation is dropped rather than corrected, because no registry in this repo carries Jescar part numbers (FretProfile.jescar is declared but empty for all six profiles), so it could not be verified; the comment says so rather than leaving the removal silent. default=0.58, ge=0.1 and le=3.0 are unchanged.
diff_articulation.why_not_redundant: This is the only occurrence of the wrong wording in the repo - git grep for 'medium fret wire tang', '47104' and '0148' each return this one file. The field is consumed by cam/fret_slots_from_ecosphere.py and by every generated fretboard, so its description is the only in-code statement of what the number means; a reader who takes 'tang' literally reaches the wrong wire.

commands_run: git grep -l 'medium fret wire tang' -> exactly one file, this one; same for '47104' and '0148'
git grep of services/api/tests for slot_width_mm -> tests assert values (0.58 / 0.56 / 0.70 / 0.1), never the description string; no snapshot or contract file pins it
python compile() of the modified module -> PASS
regex check that the Field signature is byte-identical before and after -> default=0.58, ge=0.1, le=3.0 unchanged
collateral check: src.replace(OLD,'@@') == out.replace(NEW,'@@') -> nothing outside the anchor differs
assertion that '47104', '0148' and 'fret wire tang' appear nowhere inside the Field call (they remain in the comment above it, deliberately, to record what was removed)

extracted fret_wire_physics.FRET_PROFILES -> slot_width_in 0.023in for vintage_narrow / vintage_medium / medium / medium_jumbo / tall_narrow, 0.025in for jumbo; stewmac 148 = vintage_medium, stewmac 150 = medium

files.intent: Say what 0.58mm actually is, and stop the slot/tang conflation at its source.
files.behavior_change: none - the Field description string and a preceding comment. The validated default and bounds are unchanged, so no request, response or generated fretboard differs.

architecture_scan.acknowledgement_notes: Documentation only. Kept separate from SG_FRET_WIRE_MEDIUM on purpose: that patch records a Smart Guitar product ruling in a spec file, this one corrects a shared calculator module that every instrument uses. The description text is not referenced by any test or contract snapshot, so this cannot move a gate.
